title: Mindfulness is here
hookLine: don't envy, don't hate, don't turn your backs; mindfulness is here, he said, pointing to his chest three times
tomorrow: you help a friend through a bad week. who's helping you?
last: GUARD THE TONGUE · SILENCE IS MERCY TOO · WANT LESS

cards: Everyone keeps a version of themselves for the camera: the clean desk, the good angle, the caption that sounds kind. Yesterday's question: he pointed at his chest three times; at what?
In hadith thirty-five, from Sahih Muslim, the Prophet, peace be upon him, lists what tears people apart. Don't envy each other. Don't hate each other.
Don't turn your backs on each other. Be servants of Allah, brothers. Then he says: taqwa is here, and points to his chest.

teach.h: TAQWA: A GUARD KEPT ON YOURSELF.
teach.b: Taqwa is hard to put in one English word: mindfulness of Allah, God-consciousness, a guard kept on yourself. Look at where he puts it.

teach.h: THE LIST IS OUT IN THE OPEN.
teach.b: Everything on his list happens between people, out in the open: envy, hatred, turned backs, cheating on a sale.

teach.h: THE SOURCE IS IN THE CHEST.
teach.b: And the source of all of it, he says, is in a place no camera reaches. Then, right after pointing, a hard line: it's evil enough for a person to look down on his brother.
One wording in the same collection makes the point sharper: Allah doesn't look at your bodies or your faces, but at your hearts. That's the line to tell a friend tonight. Now hold up the week.
Leave the silences alone. Want less. Start no harm.
Prove it first. At least with the heart.
Six lines, and every one of them is what taqwa in the chest looks like from the outside.

how: Muslims often quote 'taqwa is here' with a hand on the chest; teachers use this hadith to speak about envy, cutting people off and looking down on others as matters of the heart.

o: a calm spot in the mosque set apart for prayer
God-consciousness lives in the heart, not the show
a breathing exercise to slow down a racing mind

p: mindfulness of Allah, a guard on yourself
to look down on your brother

s: taqwa shows in how religious someone looks
the Prophet pointed to his chest: taqwa is here, where no one can see.
in hadith thirty-five, the Prophet points to his chest three times
taqwa is here, said with a hand on the chest.
the list in this hadith is about rare, dramatic sins
it's everyday stuff: envy, hate, turned backs, cheating on a sale.

games.q: two teammates won't sit together after a fight. the coach says, as long as they play well, who cares. what does hadith thirty-five add?
o: playing well is what counts; the rest is private.
turning your backs on each other is on the list itself.
make them sit together, whatever they feel.
games.why: don't turn your backs on each other is part of the hadith, and its source is in the chest, not the scoreboard.

practice: Rest your right hand flat on your chest. Three times, slowly, press lightly, once for each time he pointed.
Then leave the hand there for the sit and feel it rise and fall, no camera, no caption, just the place the hadith points to.

wordCard.voice: Mindfulness is here: the Prophet's words with his hand on his chest. Taqwa lives inside, and shows up in how people treat each other.

orig.note: Arabic: taqwa is here. said three times, pointing to the chest.

carryVoice: Your line: taqwa is here, where no camera reaches, and it shows in how you treat people. A full week, done.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2564 (Abu Hurayrah: don't envy, don't hate, don't turn your backs; taqwa is here, pointing to his chest three times; Allah looks at your hearts)
